bib.title: DetectGPT: Zero-Shot Machine-Generated Text Detection using Probability Curvature
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 40th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202 (arXiv v2)

question: Can text sampled from an LLM be detected zero-shot, using only the source model's log probabilities, by exploiting the local curvature of its log probability function?
hypothesis: Minor rewrites of model-generated text have lower log probability under the model than the original, while rewrites of human text may go up or down (model samples lie in negative-curvature regions).
contributions: Identification and empirical validation that the curvature of a model's log probability function is more negative at model samples than at human text
DetectGPT, a practical algorithm that approximates the trace of the log probability function's Hessian to detect a model's samples

method.summary: For a candidate passage, DetectGPT draws k perturbations with an off-the-shelf T5 mask-filling model, scores the original and perturbed passages with the source model, and thresholds the variance-normalised gap between the original log probability and the mean perturbed log probability. No training, no labelled data, no watermark.
method.task: zero-shot detection of text sampled from a given source LLM (white-box log-prob access)

datasets.name: XSum
datasets.preprocessing: machine text generated by prompting with first 30 tokens of the real article

datasets.name: PubMedQA
datasets.source: Jin et al. 2019; long-form answers by human experts
datasets.preprocessing: prompt is the question tokens only

models.name: T5-3B (T5-11B for GPT-NeoX and GPT-3; mT5-3B for WMT)
models.architecture: mask-filling perturbation model, off the shelf, no fine-tuning

models.name: OpenAI RoBERTa-base and RoBERTa-large GPT-2 detectors
models.architecture: supervised, fine-tuned on millions of GPT-2 samples

inference.decoding: machine samples drawn from the raw conditional distribution with temperature 1; also top-k (k=40) and nucleus (p=0.96) in Sec 5.2
inference.temperature: 1 for source-model sampling and for T5 mask-filling
inference.samples: 100 perturbations per passage (converges at 100); evaluation sets of 500 (Table 1), 200 (Fig 4, 6, 7), 150 (Table 2), 100 (Fig 8); single run, no seeds stated
inference.prompting: source model prompted with first 30 tokens of real text (question tokens for PubMedQA)

parameters.normalisation: divide discrepancy by std of perturbed log probs (about +0.020 AUROC)
parameters.decision_threshold: slightly below 0.1 separates human and model text across domains (Fig 9)

metrics.name: AUROC
metrics.definition: probability that a classifier ranks a random machine-generated example above a random human-written one; equal numbers of positives and negatives

baselines: OpenAI RoBERTa-base and RoBERTa-large supervised detectors
eval.protocol: 150 to 500 examples per experiment; single AUROC per cell; no confidence intervals except standard error over datasets in Fig 6

limits: White-box assumption: needs log probabilities of the source model; for API models evaluating probabilities costs money (Limitations).
Needs a reasonable perturbation function; domains where mask-filling models represent rephrases poorly lose performance; PubMedQA lower possibly for this reason.
More compute-intensive than baselines: needs sampling and scoring of about 100 perturbations per passage.
Detection is weaker when the scoring model differs from the source model (Fig 6), so it is best suited to white-box use.
For very long passages performance may fall because T5 fails to track 20+ masks at once.
Supervised detectors are as good or better in-distribution (English news).
Evaluates only sampled base models (GPT-2 to GPT-3, Jurassic-2); ChatGPT is named as not scorable; RLHF models not tested; text edited by paraphrase only simulated with T5 replacements.
Authors cite Sadasivan et al. 2023 and Krishna et al. 2023 that paraphrasing evades detectors, left as future work; relationship between prompting and detection unexplored.

terms.definition: d(x, p_theta, q) = log p_theta(x) - E over x~ drawn from q(.|x) of log p_theta(x~)
detecting whether a candidate passage is a sample from a source model without assuming access to human-written or generated samples
the detector may evaluate the log probability of a sample; it does not assume access to model architecture or parameters
